intervals.label: data taking
intervals.note: Day precision from the 1985 ICRC paper (OCR text layer: 'It has been running since June 1st, 1982 in a cave aside the Mont Blanc Tunnel'); the 1983 AIP proceedings say 'operating since 1982'. The same paper reports 2.8 years of operation by 1985. The end of data taking is not given in any source consulted; see the next interval.
intervals.quote: June 1st, 1982 In a cave aside the Mont Blanc Tunnel

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Terminal event with an unknown date, given as a window: the earliest bound (March 1985) is June 1982 plus the '2.8 years of operation' of the 1985 ICRC paper, i.e. the detector was still running then; the latest bound (July 2004) is the review (arXiv v1, 26 Jul 2004) saying NUSEX 'stopped data-taking'. No fetched source dates the end; later NUSEX analysis papers (EPL 8, 611, received 22 November 1988) show the analysis continued into 1988-89.
intervals.quote: We note that NUSEX, Fréjus, Soudan, Kamiokande and IMB stopped data-taking and currently only Superkamiokande is active.

start.display: between March 1985 and July 2004; end of data taking not stated in any source consulted

placements.note: Start date from the 1985 ICRC paper (see the experiment record). The cave position inside the tunnel is not surveyed.
placements.quote: is situated half way along the road tunnel under Mont Blanc linking France and Italy

summary.plain: A cube of iron plates 3.5 metres on a side, interleaved with layers of gas-filled plastic tubes that light up along the tracks of charged particles, weighing 150 tons.
summary.technical: 136 horizontal iron plates (1 cm, 3.5 m x 3.5 m) interleaved with planes of 320 resistive-cathode PVC streamer tubes (1 cm^2) read out by two orthogonal sets of aluminium strips; 150 t total.

technology.quote: NUSEX[3] was composed of iron plates interleaved with streamer tubes.
technology.value: Digital tracking calorimeter of iron plates interleaved with plastic streamer tubes
